title: OpenAI may be in cost control mode
lede: A post built on battle-system data argues OpenAI tuned Astra 6.2 and Sol 6.2 for cost, since both now reason and output far less per task than the models they face.

points: The authors compare each model's spend and reasoning with its opponents in the same battle, plotted against their Elo leaderboard.
Astra 6 and Sol 6.1 looked typical; the 6.2 releases stand out as outliers on reasoning and output tokens.
Reported p-values for the drop in reasoning are 0.00013 for Sol and 0.0064 for Astra.
The authors conclude both models now underthink compared with their predecessors.

points.text: One commenter calls it a single data point, arguing Astra 6.2 was a timed release that may simply be undercooked.
Others read it as OpenAI aiming for the cost-intelligence Pareto frontier on benchmarks, which suits buyers paying API rates.
A commenter notes fewer reasoning tokens could also come from better pre-training, and calls the post too sure of itself.
Several users report weaker results lately, including a team that moved from Claude to Codex for cost and found the 6.x models poor at coding.
